title: Real-time Monitoring of High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) Ablation of In Vitro Canine Livers Using Harmonic Motion Imaging for Focused Ultrasound (HMIFU)
protocol: Degas an ex vivo canine liver sample for 90 minutes.
Place the degassed liver sample in a tank filled with degassed Phosphate Buffered Solution.
Fix the liver sample on an acoustic absorber using needles at its extremities.

Insert a 64-element, 0.32 mm pitch, 2.5 MHz center frequency phased array through a circular hole located in the center of a 93-element hemispherical array HIFU transducer with a 4.5 MHz center frequency, 70 mm focal depth, and 1.7 mm x 0.4 mm focal size.
Align both transducers co-axially.
Fix the imaging transducer into the therapeutic transducer using adjustment screws.
Cover the HIFU transducer with a volume-controlled polyurethane membrane filled with flowing degassed water to cool it down.
Mount the transducer assembly on a computer-controlled 3-D positioner.
Connect the HIFU transducer to a function generator sending a 25 Hz amplitude modulated sine waveform with 500 mV maximum amplitude.
Connect the imaging transducer to a fully programmable ultrasound system using Matlab software.
Install software associated with the ultrasound system using the Matlab environment.
Place a 50 dB RF amplifier between the HIFU transducer and the function generator.
Place a matching network between the HIFU transducer and the function generator.

Create a polar grid in Matlab starting 50 mm from the surface of the array and 40 mm deep with a radial step of 9.625 µm and an azimuthal angle of 90°, using 128 lines, with the origin at the focus of the diverging wave.
Define the source of the diverging wave in Matlab 10.24 mm behind the array surface and centered laterally.

Create a Cartesian grid in Matlab starting 50 mm from the surface of the array and extending 40 mm deep in the axial direction with a step size of 9.625 µm, 20 mm wide in the lateral direction with 64 lines, for the plane wave.
Define the source of the plane wave on the surface of the array.
Compute the time from each grid point to the source and back to each element of the array for both grids.
ReconMat_DW for diverging wave imaging or ReconMat_PW for plane wave imaging in the Matlab command window and press "Enter".
Apply the delay-and-sum algorithm to each vector of the standard basis.
Retrieve non-zero elements from the resulting matrix.
Allocate non-zero elements to a sparse matrix at corresponding locations.
Save the reconstruction matrix on the computer hard drive.
Cast the reconstruction matrix to a GPU matrix.
SetUpP4_2Flash_4B_streaming_DW for diverging wave imaging or SetUpP4_2Flash_4B_streaming_PW for plane wave imaging in the Matlab command window and press "Enter".
Name the setup file “P4-2Flash_DivergingWave.mat” for diverging wave imaging.
Name the setup file “P4-2Flash_PlaneWave.mat” for plane wave imaging.
Synchronize the ultrasound system with the function generator using an external trigger.
Open Matlab.
Run the setup script “SetUpP4_2Flash_4B.m”.
Name the created setup file: “P4-2Flash_4B_Bmode.mat”.
Use the “VSX” command in Matlab.
When prompted, enter the name of the setup file “P4-2Flash_4B_Bmode.mat”.
Move both transducers and use the B-mode display to position them in the targeted region of the liver for ablation.
Target a region approximately 1 cm under the surface of the liver to avoid high ultrasound attenuation due to absorption.
Save a conventional B-mode image of the liver on the computer.
Open Matlab.
Use the “VSX” command and enter the setup file name “P4-2Flash_DivergingWave.mat” for diverging wave imaging or “P4-2Flash_PlaneWave.mat” for plane wave imaging.
Start the HIFU and apply it during 2 minutes to the targeted region.
Acquire the RF channel data at 1,000 frames per second during 2 minutes using diverging waves.
Alternatively, acquire the RF channel data at 1,000 frames per second during 2 minutes using plane waves.
Transfer the data to a host computer every 200 frames via a PCI express cable.
Alternatively, acquire RF channel data at 167 frames per second during 2 minutes using plane waves.
Transfer the acquired data to a host computer every 2 frames for real-time streaming.
Cast the RF channel data matrix to a single precision GPU matrix with Matlab.
Multiply the RF channel data matrix by the reconstruction matrix to obtain reconstructed RF data.
Create a 6th order Butterworth low pass filter at 4 MHz cutoff frequency using the DSP System Toolbox of Matlab.
Apply this low pass filter to the reconstructed RF data to filter out the 4.5 MHz HIFU component.
Estimate the axial displacement between consecutive frames using 1-D normalized cross-correlation with a 3.1mm-window length and 90% overlap.
Create a 6th order Butterworth low pass filter at 100 Hz cutoff frequency using the DSP System Toolbox of Matlab.
Apply this low pass filter to the temporal displacement data using Matlab to retrieve the 50 Hz-oscillatory frequency component.
Define a region of interest (ROI) as the focal region at -6 dB and located 70 mm away from the transducer surface.
Extract the displacement data in this ROI.

Estimate the displacement signal-to-noise ratio (SNRd) at the focal region after 2 min of ablation as the ratio between the mean displacement and the standard deviation of the displacement in the ROI.
Extract the 50 Hz temporal displacement signal at the focus from the displacement matrix data.
Convert the temporal displacement signal at the focus into audible sound using Matlab.
